whyCheapBearCase.answer: FDX is not statistically cheap (P/E 17.54, P/B 2.47), and quant signals are actually favorable - positive sentiment (0.375) and a strong analyst score (72.1) [source: 1] - yet the stock is down -13.53% over 3 months and -8.02% over 6 months [source: 1], despite full-year FY2026 (ended May 31, 2026) net income, operating income, and diluted EPS all growing versus FY2025 [source: 4]. The filings surface several concrete, filing-confirmed sources of uncertainty that plausibly explain market caution despite improving trailing results. First, in November 2025 the FAA issued an emergency Airworthiness Directive prohibiting further flight of all Boeing MD-11 aircraft (a type FedEx operates in its cargo fleet) until inspection and corrective action; the Q3 FY2026 10-Q states FedEx 'cannot reasonably estimate the financial impact, and no adjustments have been recorded' [source: 2]. Second, following the U.S. Supreme Court's February 20, 2026 decision invalidating IEEPA tariffs, FedEx has recorded a $749 million customer-refund liability as of May 31, 2026, and faces 14 nationwide class action lawsuits (13 consolidated in Tennessee federal court, one in the Court of International Trade) seeking tariff refunds from FedEx, with the financial impact still 'uncertain' [source: 3]. Third, FedEx is executing a planned spin-off of FedEx Freight - already financed via new FedEx Freight Holding Company senior notes priced February 5, 2026 and a new revolving/delayed-draw credit facility from January 15, 2026 - alongside a ~$2.6 billion InPost S.A. consortium investment (FedEx to hold 37%) whose 'strategic or financial benefits' management explicitly cannot guarantee will be achieved [source: 2, 3]. Together these are real, dated, unresolved execution and legal risks layered on top of otherwise-improving results.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Improving on a full fiscal-year basis, per SEC XBRL data. FY2026 (ended May 31, 2026) net income was $4,433 million versus $4,092 million in FY2025, up 8.3%; operating income was $5,463 million versus $5,217 million, up 4.7%; diluted EPS was $18.55 versus $16.81, up 10.4% (EPS growing faster than net income, consistent with buyback activity) [source: 4]. I was NOT able to verify the revenue trend from XBRL: the extracted 'Revenues' tag data in this packet has no FY2026 or FY2025 data points (its most recent values are stale, from 2018-2019), so a same-tag YoY revenue comparison is not determinable from the sources available to this pass [source: 4]. I also flag a genuine, unresolved internal discrepancy: this project's own companyMetrics reports epsGrowth of -91.39%, which sharply contradicts the +10.4% FY2026 diluted-EPS growth computed directly above from SEC XBRL data [source: 1, 4]. I cannot reconcile this difference from the sources available in this pass (it may reflect a different period basis, such as a single quarter versus full fiscal year, or a data artifact in the quant pipeline) and am disclosing it rather than picking one figure as authoritative. For the first nine months of FY2026 (through February 28, 2026), net income was $2,836 million and operating income was $3,912 million, implying Q4 FY2026 alone contributed roughly $1,597 million of net income and $1,551 million of operating income by subtraction - a strong closing quarter, though this is a derived, not directly reported, figure [source: 4].

marginTrend.answer: Not cleanly determinable from the filing text captured in this pass. Because the revenue XBRL trend data does not include current-period FY2026/FY2025 figures (see above), I cannot compute an operating-margin percentage for FY2026 directly from XBRL [source: 4]. This project's own companyMetrics reports operatingMargin of 5.77% and marginTrend of -0.16 (slightly declining) [source: 1], which is directionally plausible for FedEx's typically thin, capital-intensive margin profile, but I could not independently verify it from the extracted MD&A text: the .mda.text field for both filings had located:true but actually captured boilerplate (the 10-Q's field captured the Exhibit Index/Signature page; the 10-K's captured the auditor's internal-control report) rather than the Results of Operations revenue/expense narrative. Operating income did grow more slowly than net income and diluted EPS on a percentage basis (operating income +4.7% vs. net income +8.3% and EPS +10.4%) [source: 4], weakly suggesting core operating performance grew more modestly than what flowed through to shareholders (likely aided by buybacks and/or below-the-line items), but without a verified revenue figure this cannot be stated as a clean margin conclusion. The 10-K's keyword-scan hits separately reference noncash 'Asset Impairment Charges' tied to permanently retiring certain aircraft and engines, recorded in both FY2026 and FY2025, which a full margin analysis would need to isolate but which I could not quantify from the extracted text alone [source: 3].

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from available sources. The extracted MD&A text for both filings captured the wrong sections (auditor's internal-control report for the 10-K; exhibit index and signature page for the 10-Q) rather than the actual 'Outlook' discussion that the filings' own cross-references indicate exists (keywordScan hits reference an 'Outlook' heading under Results of Operations and a separate 'Liquidity Outlook' section, but the content itself was not captured) [source: 2, 3]. No cached news headline in this packet addresses FedEx guidance specifically. I am not inventing a guidance direction from the section headers alone.

catalysts.text: FY2026 full-year net income (+8.3%), operating income (+4.7%), and diluted EPS (+10.4%) all grew versus FY2025 - a genuinely improving profitability trend as of the most recent fiscal year-end.

Consortium investment in InPost S.A. (FedEx holding 37% post-close, ~$2.6 billion) expanding FedEx's exposure to European parcel-locker/last-mile delivery infrastructure, expected to complete in the second half of 2026.

Planned FedEx Freight spin-off, already financed with dedicated FedEx Freight Holding Company debt (new senior notes priced February 5, 2026 across four tranches, plus a new revolving credit and delayed-draw term loan facility from January 15, 2026), intended to sharpen the strategic focus of the remaining business and potentially unlock separate valuation for the standalone LTL freight unit.

Continued technology/automation investment referenced in cached news around robotics and trailer-loading automation at FedEx's Hagerstown hub, plus an AI-driven assistant launched within the FedEx Developer Portal (May 2026) to accelerate integrations with FedEx digital services.

risks.text: FAA emergency Airworthiness Directive (November 2025) grounding all Boeing MD-11 aircraft pending inspection - a real, current operational disruption to FedEx's air cargo fleet with financial impact the company explicitly states it 'cannot reasonably estimate' as of the Q3 FY2026 10-Q.

Unresolved IEEPA tariff litigation: 14 nationwide class action lawsuits (13 consolidated in Tennessee federal court, one in the Court of International Trade) seeking tariff refunds from FedEx following the Supreme Court's February 20, 2026 invalidation of IEEPA tariffs; FedEx has already recorded a $749 million customer-refund liability as of May 31, 2026, with the ultimate financial impact still uncertain.

Planned FedEx Freight spin-off carries explicitly disclosed execution risk: 'the business and network integration and optimization process could result in higher-than-currently-expected costs, less-than-expected savings, the loss of customers, the disruption of ongoing businesses, union organizing, litigation, legal disputes with service providers, governmental agency challenges,' per the 10-K's own risk disclosure, plus potential asset impairment charges.

InPost investment success depends on the actions of other consortium investors and InPost's own management, since FedEx would hold a minority (37%) stake and 'may not be able to influence key strategic or operational decisions'; the deal also remains subject to regulatory approvals with no guarantee of completion or of achieving expected benefits.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence leans toward 'opportunity': FY2026 net income, operating income, and diluted EPS all grew YoY [source: 4], and the quant signals (positive sentiment, above-average analyst score of 72.1) [source: 1] are not consistent with a market that has lost confidence in the business - yet the stock has still fallen -13.53%/-8.02% over 3/6 months [source: 1]. That gap is at least partly explained by several real, filing-confirmed, currently-unresolved items: the MD-11 fleet grounding with unquantified financial impact, the still-uncertain IEEPA tariff litigation with a $749 million liability already recorded, and FedEx Freight spin-off execution risk plus potential impairment charges [source: 2, 3] - genuine structural and legal uncertainty layered on top of otherwise-improving trailing fundamentals, rather than either a clean opportunity or a clean value trap. Confidence is medium rather than higher because of significant data-quality gaps specific to this ticker's extraction: the revenue XBRL tag data was stale/missing for FY2026 (so revenue trend and operating margin could not be independently verified), the filings' own 'Outlook' section content was never actually captured despite being cross-referenced, and this project's own companyMetrics epsGrowth figure (-91.39%) directly contradicts the +10.4% EPS growth computed from XBRL - three separate, unresolved limitations that leave real uncertainty about how strongly this should be read as an opportunity versus a value trap.
